comparator.name: Bachelor Mechanical Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 Mechanical Engineering/Marine Technology OER curriculum table (PDF page index 25), rechecked on 15 October 2026, establishes the 25 stored components and their 180-EC total. Each of Years 1 and 2 contains ten 6-EC units. Year 1 separately credits Design Projects 1, 2, 3A and 3B; the public page groups 3A and 3B as one third design project. Year 2 contains four project units: Advanced Engineering Design, Process Engineering and Thermodynamics, Robotics, and Materials Science. Year 3 preserves the approved 30-EC minor and requires Systems and Control Engineering 6 EC, Integrated Mechanical Systems 6 EC, Engineer and Society 4 EC and the Bachelor Final Project 14 EC. Mathematics/mechanics subparts remain within their credited parent units. No named route requires selection. The previously verified component identities, weights and neutral route decision are preserved.

alternatives.labelRationale: The curriculum combines mathematical and data methods with environmental systems, geothermal/resource investigation, circular recovery and renewable-system assessment. These are specific sustainable-technology studies, without claims to mechanical thermodynamics, structural materials or manufacturing engineering.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Seven courses (52.5 EC) differ in each direction. Logic, networks, algorithms, optimisation, robotics, AI decisions and reinforcement learning give way to Dynamic Earth, Earth-system tools, soils/aquifers, climate science, environmental biogeochemistry, resource recovery and advanced resource research. This shifts the substantive focus from autonomous computation to renewable technology and circular resource systems.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The strongest complete related response develops mathematical, computational, robotic and product-development methods; it does not reproduce the mechanical-science core. The independently evidenced energy-efficiency and circularity direction supports a second curriculum with seven substantively different courses. Structural materials/manufacturing was then rejected because the workbook lacks solid mechanics, mechanics of materials, engineering-materials testing and manufacturing-process progression; introductory materials in Sustainability Essentials II and one Consumer Product Design project cannot supply that spine. Thermal/fluid engineering was assessed separately: renewable-energy assessment and soils/aquifer investigation do not supply thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat-transfer theory or thermal-system laboratories. Neither direction supports a third complete coherent 24-course programme.

notes.text: These UCR programmes offer related mathematical, autonomous-system, product-development and sustainable-resource studies. They do not reproduce statics, mechanics of materials, mechanical dynamics, thermodynamics, fluid flow and heat transfer, engineering materials/manufacturing, mechanical laboratories, integrated control hardware or the cumulative mechanical-design and final-project sequence.

Selected course content, profiles, formal prerequisites and exact planned terms were checked against the current GitHub data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879. All 151 rows were inspected for possible coherent directions; courses without planned availability were excluded.
